es: Redactar un calendario y un presupuesto con hitos, marcadores de plazo (by, no later than, within) y futuros precisos.

teaching.en: The first milestone is the venue contract, which we will have signed by the end of March, well before the busy summer season begins.
teaching.es: El primer hito es el contrato del local, que habremos firmado para finales de marzo, mucho antes de que empiece la temporada alta de verano.
teaching.explanationEs: Milestone = hito del calendario; by + fecha va con futuro perfecto: la acción estará hecha.
segments: The first milestone is the venue contract, which we will have signed
by the end of March, well before the busy summer season begins.
teaching.audioText: The first milestone is the venue contract, which we will have signed by the end of March, well before the busy summer season begins.

teaching.en: We will have paid the insurance fee no later than 15 April, because the company needs two weeks of lead time to issue the policy.
teaching.es: Habremos pagado la cuota del seguro como muy tarde el 15 de abril, porque la compañía necesita dos semanas de antelación para emitir la póliza.
teaching.explanationEs: No later than + fecha = plazo máximo; lead time es el tiempo previo que exige un trámite.
segments: We will have paid the insurance fee no later than 15 April, because
the company needs two weeks of lead time to issue the policy.
teaching.audioText: We will have paid the insurance fee no later than 15 April, because the company needs two weeks of lead time to issue the policy.

teaching.en: Within two weeks of the contract being signed, we will be advertising the festival in schools, shops and local newspapers.
teaching.es: En las dos semanas siguientes a la firma del contrato, estaremos promocionando el festival en colegios, tiendas y periódicos locales.
teaching.explanationEs: Within + plazo da el margen; el futuro continuo (will be advertising) describe lo que estará en marcha.
segments: Within two weeks of the contract being signed, we will
be advertising the festival in schools, shops and local newspapers.
teaching.audioText: Within two weeks of the contract being signed, we will be advertising the festival in schools, shops and local newspapers.

teaching.en: We will allocate 3,000 dollars to the music and earmark 800 for advertising, so that no cost overrun can touch the prize money.
teaching.es: Destinaremos 3.000 dólares a la música y reservaremos 800 para publicidad, de modo que ningún sobrecosto pueda tocar el dinero de los premios.
teaching.explanationEs: Allocate X to Y reparte el dinero; earmark lo reserva para un fin; overrun es el gasto que supera lo previsto.
segments: We will allocate 3,000 dollars to the music and earmark 800 for
advertising, so that no cost overrun can touch the prize money.
teaching.audioText: We will allocate 3,000 dollars to the music and earmark 800 for advertising, so that no cost overrun can touch the prize money.

teaching.en: If we stay on schedule, we will have been preparing for six months when the gates open, but if we fall behind schedule, we will postpone the opening.
teaching.es: Si seguimos el calendario, habremos estado preparándonos durante seis meses cuando se abran las puertas, pero si nos retrasamos, aplazaremos la apertura.
teaching.explanationEs: Will have been + -ing mide cuánto tiempo llevas haciendo algo; behind schedule = con retraso.
segments: If we stay on schedule, we will have been preparing for six months when
the gates open, but if we fall behind schedule, we will postpone the opening.
teaching.audioText: If we stay on schedule, we will have been preparing for six months when the gates open, but if we fall behind schedule, we will postpone the opening.

teaching.en: A contingency fund of ten per cent will cover any overrun, and the treasurer will sign off each payment before it leaves the account.
teaching.es: Un fondo de contingencia del diez por ciento cubrirá cualquier sobrecosto, y el tesorero dará el visto bueno a cada pago antes de que salga de la cuenta.
teaching.explanationEs: Contingency fund: dinero reservado para imprevistos; se menciona al final del presupuesto.
segments: A contingency fund of ten per cent will cover any overrun, and
the treasurer will sign off each payment before it leaves the account.
teaching.audioText: A contingency fund of ten per cent will cover any overrun, and the treasurer will sign off each payment before it leaves the account.

prompt.es: Elige la frase correcta: «Para el 31 de marzo habremos firmado el contrato.»

choices.text: By 31 March we will have signed the venue contract.
Until 31 March we will have signed the venue contract.
By 31 March we will have been signing the venue contract.

feedback.es: By + fecha con futuro perfecto indica que la acción estará terminada para ese momento; until y el perfecto continuo no expresan un plazo límite.

hint.es: By marca el plazo límite; se combina con will have + participio.

origin.text: Plan: the venue contract is signed on 28 March. The council meets on 31 March and expects the contract to be ready by then.

prompt.es: Completa: «En las dos semanas siguientes a la firma estaremos promocionando el festival.»

feedback.es: Within + plazo indica el margen máximo: within two weeks = dentro de dos semanas.

hint.es: Es la preposición que da un margen de tiempo, sin of.

origin.text: The posters are urgent. ___ two weeks of signing the contract, we will be advertising the festival in schools and shops.

answer.text: We will allocate 500 dollars to the insurance

feedback.es: Allocate + cantidad + to + destino: reparte el dinero entre partidas.

hint.es: Empieza con el futuro will y deja el destino del dinero para el final.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige por qué debe pagarse el seguro con tanta antelación.

choices.text: Because the contract cannot be signed without it.
Because the company needs time to prepare the policy.
Because the fee rises after the end of March.

feedback.es: Carlos explica que la compañía necesita dos semanas de antelación (lead time); el texto no une el seguro a la firma ni habla de una subida de precio.

origin.audio: Carlos presented the festival schedule to the volunteers on Tuesday. The first milestone, he explained, is the venue contract, which must be signed by the end of March. No later than the fifteenth of April, the insurance fee will have been paid, because the company needs two weeks of lead time. Within two weeks of signing the contract, the team will be advertising in schools and shops. He warned that if the project fell behind schedule at any stage, the opening would have to be postponed.

prompt.es: Completa: «Si nos retrasamos sobre el calendario, aplazaremos la apertura.»

feedback.es: Fall behind schedule = retrasarse respecto al calendario; ahead of schedule sería lo contrario.

origin.text: The schedule is tight. If we fall ___ schedule at any stage, we will postpone the opening by a week.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada palabra del calendario y del presupuesto con su significado.

feedback.es: Cada término ordena un aspecto: el hito fija fechas, allocate reparte dinero, lead time mide la antelación y overrun el sobrecosto.

prompt.es: Escucha el mensaje de Carlos. ¿Qué opina del presupuesto de música?

choices.text: That it is generous enough to leave some money over.
That it should be cut to protect the insurance payment.
That it is unlikely to cover the real cost of the music.

feedback.es: El grupo cuesta 3.400 frente a 3.000 reservados, y el equipo suele sufrir sobrecostos: Carlos teme que no alcance.

origin.audio: Hi Ana, it's Carlos about the festival budget. I have checked the figures, and I am afraid the music budget is too hopeful. We have earmarked 3,000 dollars, but the band's fee is 3,400, and sound equipment usually brings a cost overrun. If we pay the insurance after the tickets go on sale, we could cover the difference without touching the reserve. Let me know what you think before Friday.

prompt.es: ¿Qué problema anticipa la autora de este mensaje?

choices.text: A lack of money in the weeks before the second payment.
A delay in the council's decision on the grant this spring.
A rise in the price charged by the printers for the posters.

feedback.es: Gastará casi todo antes del segundo pago de la subvención y por eso pide no firmar nuevos contratos; el mensaje no habla de retrasos del consejo ni de subidas de precio.

origin.text: Dear all, the council will pay the grant in two parts: half in April and half after the festival. Since the insurance must be paid by 15 April, and the printers want payment before they start, we will have spent almost everything before the second payment arrives. I suggest that nobody sign any new contract until we know exactly what the council will give.

prompt.es: Completa: «Habremos estado preparando el festival durante seis meses.»

feedback.es: Will have been + -ing con for + duración mide cuánto tiempo lleváis: for six months.

origin.text: The first planning meeting took place in March. By the time the gates open in September, we will have been preparing the festival ___ six months.

prompt.es: Escribe el calendario del festival: tres hitos con fechas y un presupuesto breve.

answer.text: Our timeline for the Moon Festival is clear. By 31 March we will have signed the contract with the venue, and this is our first milestone. No later than 15 April we will have paid the insurance fee, because the company needs two weeks of lead time. Within a month of that date we will be advertising the festival in schools and shops, and the posters will be on every street by the end of May. If we stay on schedule, we will have been preparing for six months when the gates open on 12 September. The budget is 6,000 dollars. We will allocate 3,000 dollars to the music, 500 to the insurance and 800 to advertising. We will earmark the remaining 1,700 dollars as a contingency fund, so that no overrun can put the festival at risk. In this way, every volunteer will know what to do, and the council will see that our plan is serious, realistic and ready to start.
accepted: Our timeline for the Moon Festival is clear. By 31 March we will have signed the contract with the venue, and this is our first milestone. No later than 15 April we will have paid the insurance fee, because the company needs two weeks of lead time. Within a month of that date we will be advertising the festival in schools and shops, and the posters will be on every street by the end of May. If we stay on schedule, we will have been preparing for six months when the gates open on 12 September. The budget is 6,000 dollars. We will allocate 3,000 dollars to the music, 500 to the insurance and 800 to advertising. We will earmark the remaining 1,700 dollars as a contingency fund, so that no overrun can put the festival at risk. In this way, every volunteer will know what to do, and the council will see that our plan is serious, realistic and ready to start.

First, the venue: we will have signed the contract by 31 March, which is our first milestone. Second, the insurance: no later than 15 April we will have paid the fee, because the company needs time to issue the policy. Third, the promotion: within three weeks we will be advertising in every school and shop, and by the time the festival opens, we will have been working on it for half a year. Our budget is 6,000 dollars in total. We will allocate 3,000 dollars to the music, 500 dollars to the insurance and 800 dollars to advertising, and we will keep 1,700 dollars as a contingency fund in case of an overrun. With this schedule and this budget, the council can be sure that the festival is feasible and that nobody will pay more than planned.

feedback.es: Un buen calendario ordena los hitos con by, no later than y within, usa will have + participio o will be + -ing y reparte el dinero con allocate o earmark.

origin.text: Festival de la Luna, 12 de septiembre. Contrato del local: firmado el 31 de marzo. Seguro: pagado el 15 de abril como plazo máximo. Carteles: en colegios y tiendas durante mayo. Presupuesto: 6.000 dólares (música 3.000, seguro 500, publicidad 800, reserva 1.700). Escribe en inglés unas 190–240 palabras: tres hitos con futuro perfecto o continuo y un presupuesto breve.

prompt.es: Escucha la noticia. ¿Qué sugiere la decisión de la tesorera?

choices.text: That the festival will probably be cancelled if the delay continues.
That the delay is being handled with money already set aside.
That the printers will return part of their fee to the team.

feedback.es: Usar la reserva para publicidad extra indica que el retraso se gestiona con dinero ya previsto; la noticia no habla de cancelar ni de reembolsos.

origin.audio: The organisers of a street festival said yesterday that they had fallen behind schedule. The printers needed more lead time than expected, so the posters will reach the shops a week later than planned. To avoid a cost overrun, the treasurer has earmarked part of the reserve for extra advertising online.

prompt.es: ¿Qué muestra la reserva de 1.700 dólares sobre el enfoque de los organizadores?

choices.text: That they plan to spend the reserve on better music equipment.
That they are unsure whether the festival will take place.
That they expect some costs to go above their estimates.

feedback.es: Una reserva de imprevistos indica que prevén que algún costo supere lo calculado; el texto no dice que la reserva vaya a la música.

origin.text: Milestone 1: venue contract signed by 31 March. Milestone 2: insurance paid no later than 15 April. Milestone 3: posters in schools and shops within two weeks of the contract. Budget: 3,000 dollars to music, 500 to insurance, 800 to advertising and 1,700 in reserve.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Habremos pagado la cuota como muy tarde el día cinco.»

answer.text: We will have paid the fee no later than the fifth

feedback.es: No later than + fecha marca el plazo máximo; se combina con el futuro perfecto will have paid.
